category.name: Team chat
category.description: Persistent team messaging, channels, direct messages, and collaborative conversations.
category.audience: Employees and external collaborators across business functions and industries.
category.audienceRationale: A cross-functional communication need shared by distributed and office-based teams; reach ranking is qualitative, not a headcount estimate.

pricing.note: Pro standard annual price per user/month; free plan available; temporary introductory discount excluded.
Teams Essentials US annual subscription; Microsoft 365 bundles and enterprise editions differ.

oss.classificationReason: All self-hosted software features included in every plan; no enterprise code tier. A applies to software, with separately priced vendor push relay disclosed.

oss.name: Mattermost Team Edition
locked: Group calling and guest accounts excluded from Team Edition.
SSO removed from Team Edition; advanced identity, permissions, compliance and HA in proprietary editions.
oss.classificationReason: Core source AGPLv3; designated webapp/admin/config folders Apache-2.0; vendor-compiled Team binary MIT. Enterprise code separately commercial. Tier C because everyday group calls/guests are gated. Proprietary Entry free mode is separate; its 10,000-message cap does not apply to Team. Vendor positions Team below 250 activated users.

Community limited app integrations and video integrations (Jitsi/BigBlueButton only); advanced identity/governance and air-gapped offering require premium plan.

alternatives.migrationNotes: Channel-plus-topic model differs from Slack threads; Slack export/import documented, private data availability depends on source export permissions.

Matrix rooms, federation and encryption differ from Slack channels and app workflows. Plan identity, integration and history transfer separately; no verified one-click importer or bridge parity claimed.

Team offers channels, DMs and core search, but no group calls or guest accounts. Current Slack migration guide targets Entry/paid editions; Team import parity requires verification; integrations must be rebuilt.
Slack importer handles users/channels/messages; attachments need a separate pending-file download step and existing usernames can be skipped. Community edition limits remain.
Beta Teams importer maps teams to channels; excludes DMs and private-channel messages. Keep Microsoft tenant active through migration; does not replace Office applications.

Matrix rooms, federation and encryption provide a different messaging architecture. Plan identities and history transfer separately; no verified one-click history importer or bridge parity claimed. Does not reproduce Microsoft 365 applications.
Partial replacement for persistent channels/DMs. Team lacks group calls and SSO; no verified Teams history importer; meetings and Office-file workflows need separate replacements.
Core messaging replacement with Community concurrency/push/integration limits. No verified Teams history import; Microsoft 365 apps and meeting workflows need separate replacements.

exclusions.name: Mattermost Entry (as OSS candidate)
exclusions.reason: Free mode of commercially licensed Enterprise binary, not the OSS Team Edition; message history capped at 10,000.

exclusions.name: Rocket.Chat Starter (as OSS candidate)
exclusions.reason: Free premium-feature offering with 50-user ceiling; distinguish from MIT Community core.

exclusions.name: Element Web alone (as complete server alternative)
exclusions.reason: Matrix client needs a homeserver; suite record uses official complete-stack repository instead.

uncertainties: Mattermost current Slack migration guide lists Entry and paid editions, omits Team; Team importer compatibility not verified.
No fully faithful Slack/Teams migration assumed: exports, identity, integrations, meetings and document-suite behavior require separate evaluation.
Rocket.Chat Community limits are documented vendor-edition behavior; MIT source rights remain distinct.
Element Community recommended scale of around 100 users is not an enforced user limit.
